scope: Checksummed bounded legacy snapshot preview with canonical people, project, task, idea, journal, memory, link, bucket and inbox migration
acceptance: A bounded gzip tar snapshot is inspected without filesystem extraction and requires one safe root, regular files only and a complete SHA-256 manifest
Preview and commit fail closed for changed bytes, unsafe paths, links, unknown manifest shapes, unsupported collection versions, fields, tombstones and domains
Reviewed people records map into the canonical PeopleStore in one SQLite transaction with a durable replay-safe receipt
Authenticated HTTP and console file selection expose verified preview, explicit supported-domain coverage, reviewed commit and persisted receipts
Version-1 memory, link, idea and journal records retain stable conflict IDs, source identity, timestamps, tags, URLs and structured provenance in one canonical KnowledgeStore transaction
One version-1 project is staged and atomically published per archive with its stable relationship ID and replay receipt in the canonical project tree
Version-1 bookmark buckets become canonical manual collections and link bucket IDs become validated relational memberships in the same KnowledgeStore transaction

Version-1 inbox records preserve stable capture IDs, meaningful routing state and immutable classification history; routed records require an existing or same-transaction canonical knowledge destination
One version-1 admin action or tracked thread is crash-safely published as a canonical native Task with stable identity, mapped work state, embedded replay receipt and validated canonical references
limits: This sub-slice supports only version-1 people, projects, admin, threads, ideas, journals, memories, links, buckets and inbox collection records; every other archive domain, relational dump and future schema is rejected.
People, project, task and knowledge archive families require separate imports so each authoritative store and its receipt publish atomically; project and task archives are limited to one record.
Shared durability inventory and final fresh-home restore integration remain owned by the root integration slice.

Song sheets and their binary attachments remain pending because the canonical music catalog does not own notation, instrument, learning stage or songbook attachments; full fresh-home restore proof also remains pending.
